orders.reason: Gait difficulty, bilateral hand numbness, hyperreflexia; evaluate for cervical myelopathy

documents.title: Office Visit - gait difficulty, hand numbness
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: "my legs aren't working right."

HPI: 60-year-old man. For about four months walking has gotten harder: he feels unsteady and holds the rail on the cab steps now. Both hands feel numb. When he bends his head forward he gets a sharp, electric pain shooting down both arms. On a few occasions he has leaked urine before he could get to a bathroom, which is new for him. No falls with injury. No fever, no recent neck trauma.

PMH: T2DM, HTN, HLD, obesity, OSA, achalasia.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg, amlodipine 5 mg, HCTZ 25 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg. NKDA.

Exam: BP 135/90, HR 74, RR 15, T 36.4, SpO2 96%. Wt 102.3 kg, BMI 32.4.
General: well, worried.
Neck: no tenderness to palpation.
Neuro: alert, speech normal. Strength grossly preserved in arms and legs. Knee and ankle reflexes brisk on both sides. Gait unsteady.
Feet: skin intact, pulses 2+, monofilament sensation present at all sites.

Assessment: Progressive gait disturbance, bilateral hand numbness, urinary leakage and neck-flexion arm pains with brisk leg reflexes. Concern for compression of the cervical spinal cord.

Plan
- MRI cervical spine without contrast, ordered; front desk to get the first available slot.
- Neurosurgery referral placed.
- Call or text right away for new weakness, falls, or loss of bladder or bowel control.
- Diabetes labs at July visit as planned.

documents.title: MRI cervical spine without contrast
documents.author: radiology
documents.body:
MRI CERVICAL SPINE WITHOUT CONTRAST
Date of exam: 06/04/2024
Indication: 4 months of progressive gait difficulty, bilateral hand numbness, urinary leakage, brisk reflexes. Evaluate for cervical myelopathy.
Technique: Multiplanar, multisequence MRI of the cervical spine without intravenous contrast.
Comparison: none.

Findings:
Alignment is maintained. Vertebral body heights are preserved. Bone marrow signal is unremarkable.
There is multilevel degenerative disc disease of the cervical spine, with disc changes at several levels narrowing the canal and compressing the spinal cord.
The craniocervical junction is normal. Visualized posterior fossa is unremarkable.
Paraspinal soft tissues are unremarkable.

Impression:
Multilevel cervical degenerative disc disease with spinal cord compression.

documents.title: MRI result reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: MRI C-spine: multilevel degenerative disc disease compressing the spinal cord. Called patient and reviewed. Neurosurgery referral is in; asked staff to push for the earliest consult and send the images and report there. Same precautions as at the visit.

documents.title: Neurosurgery appointment
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Patient called back. Neurosurgery office has him for 07/30, earliest new-patient opening; on their cancellation list. MRI disc and report sent to them 06/05 per front desk.
He says symptoms are the same as at the visit, no new weakness, no falls. Reviewed reasons to call us or go to the ED (sudden weakness, can't walk, lose control of bladder or bowels). He verbalized understanding.

documents.title: Neurosurgery consultation
documents.author: neurosurgery
documents.body:
NEUROSURGERY — NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 07/30/2024
Patient: Lamar Bryant (DOB 02/26/1964), 60-year-old man
Referred by: primary care

History: Mr. Bryant has type 2 diabetes, hypertension and hyperlipidemia, and had a work-up for swallowing difficulty a year ago. Over the past six months his walking has steadily worsened. Both hands are numb, and he has had episodes of leaking urine. Bending his neck forward sends sharp pains down his arms.

Allergies: NKDA.
Medications: metformin 1000 mg twice daily; lisinopril 20 mg daily; amlodipine 5 mg daily; hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily; atorvastatin 40 mg daily.
Past surgical history: none.
Social: long-haul truck driver. Former smoker, 20 pack-years. Alcohol 1-2 drinks per month.

Examination: Lower extremity reflexes exaggerated. Hoffmann sign present bilaterally. Gait unsteady.

Imaging: MRI of the cervical spine (06/04/2024), images reviewed today: multilevel degenerative disc disease with compression of the spinal cord.

Laboratory (primary care, 07/16/2024): HbA1c 7.2%, fasting glucose 156 mg/dL, creatinine 1.0 mg/dL, total cholesterol 210 mg/dL, BUN 14 mg/dL.

Impression: Cervical spondylotic myelopathy.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
LDCT CHEST, LUNG CANCER SCREENING
Indication: annual screening; former smoker, 20 pack-years, quit 2011.
Technique: Low-dose CT of the chest without contrast.
Comparison: 09/12/2023.
Findings:
No pulmonary nodules. No airspace disease, effusion or pneumothorax.
Esophagus remains dilated, consistent with known achalasia, similar to prior.
No thoracic lymphadenopathy. Heart size normal. Aorta normal in caliber.
Included upper abdomen and bones without suspicious finding.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1, negative. Dilated esophagus consistent with known achalasia. Next annual screening in 12 months.

Lamar Bryant, 60

Interval: Neurosurgery consultation 07/30 - diagnosed cervical spondylotic myelopathy. LDCT 09/10 Lung-RADS 1. FIT negative 02/2024. Last eye exam 08/2023.
Feels "about the same." Still working.

Problem list: type 2 diabetes (since 2004); essential hypertension; hyperlipidemia; obesity; obstructive sleep apnea (2022); achalasia (2023); cervical spondylotic myelopathy (2024); former smoker.

HEENT: normal. Neck: supple.
Heart: RRR, no murmur. Lungs: clear.
Abdomen: soft, nontender.
Extremities: no edema.

LOW-DOSE CT CHEST (LUNG CANCER SCREENING)
